content.text: The text reviews intestinal and rectal diseases, intestinal parasites, and liver disorders. Intestinal cancer commonly affects the sigmoid colon or caecum, causing pain, alternating constipation and diarrhea, obstruction, wasting, tumors, and eventual death; treatment is largely palliative, though colostomy or excision may temporarily help. Lardaceous intestinal degeneration causes late, often severe diarrhea and hemorrhage. Rectal conditions include prolapse, polyps, hemorrhoids, fissures, strictures, ulcers, abscesses, fistulae, syphilis, tuberculosis, and cancer. Treatments described include diet, laxatives, enemas, cautery, dilation, incision, excision, and artificial anus. Parasites include tapeworms, flukes, roundworms, hookworms, pinworms, trichinae, and filariae, with infection linked to undercooked meat, unsafe water, and animals. Liver sections discuss biliousness, lithaemia, glycosuria, jaundice, congestion, perihepatitis, and cirrhosis. A patient and several surgical cases were treated at or reported from the Pennsylvania Hospital.
